stateRecovery.settings.title: Cmdr couldn’t read your settings, so it started with the defaults

@stateRecovery.settings.title.description: Headline of a notice shown once at launch: Cmdr's settings file was damaged (for example by a crash or a full disk while it was being saved), so Cmdr set it aside and started with default settings. "Cmdr" is the product name. Sentence case, no full stop. Avoid the words "error" and "failed". Pop-up notice (toast) in the corner of Cmdr's main window.

stateRecovery.settings.body: Usage stats and crash reports stay off until you turn them back on in Settings › Updates & privacy.

@stateRecovery.settings.body.description: Body of the notice above. Cmdr turned two privacy settings off on purpose (the person may have turned them off before, and Cmdr can't tell any more), and this says how to turn them back on. "Settings › Updates & privacy" names the settings window and its section: keep the › separator and use the section's translated name. Plain text. Pop-up notice (toast) in the corner of Cmdr's main window.

@stateRecovery.settings.openSettings.description: Button on the notice above that opens Cmdr's Settings on the Updates & privacy section. VERB phrase, short control label. Pop-up notice (toast) in the corner of Cmdr's main window.

stateRecovery.shortcuts.title: Cmdr couldn’t read your keyboard shortcuts, so they’re back to the defaults

@stateRecovery.shortcuts.title.description: Headline of a notice shown once: the file holding the person's custom keyboard shortcuts was damaged, so Cmdr set it aside and every shortcut is back to its default key. "Cmdr" is the product name. Sentence case, no full stop. Avoid the words "error" and "failed". Pop-up notice (toast) in the corner of Cmdr's main window.

stateRecovery.license.title: Cmdr couldn’t read its license file

stateRecovery.license.body: If Cmdr shows as unlicensed now, enter your license key again in Settings › License.

@stateRecovery.license.body.description: Body of the notice above: what to do if the license no longer shows. "Settings › License" names the settings window and its section: keep the › separator and use the section's translated name. Plain text. Pop-up notice (toast) in the corner of Cmdr's main window.

@stateRecovery.license.openSettings.description: Button on the notice above that opens Cmdr's Settings on the License section. VERB phrase, short control label. Pop-up notice (toast) in the corner of Cmdr's main window.

stateRecovery.appStatus.title: Cmdr couldn’t read which folders your panes had open, so they start at your home folder

@stateRecovery.appStatus.title.description: Headline of a notice shown once at launch: the file remembering each pane's folders, tabs, and layout was damaged, so both panes open at the home folder with the default layout. "Cmdr" is the product name; a "pane" is one of the two side-by-side file lists. Sentence case, no full stop. Avoid the words "error" and "failed". Pop-up notice (toast) in the corner of Cmdr's main window.

"Cmdr" is the product name. Sentence case, no full stop. Avoid the words "error" and "failed". Pop-up notice (toast) in the corner of Cmdr's main window.

"Cmdr" is the product name. Sentence case, no full stop. Avoid the words "error" and "failed". Pop-up notice (toast) in the corner of Cmdr's main window.

stateRecovery.s3Places.title: Cmdr couldn’t read all your saved S3 places, so some may be missing

@stateRecovery.s3Places.title.description: Headline of a notice shown once: the file holding the person's saved S3 cloud storage accounts and bucket places couldn't be read, either the whole file or only some entries in it (for example ones saved by a newer Cmdr version), so some or all of them are missing from the list now. Passwords and keys are safe; they're stored elsewhere. "S3" is a technical name for this kind of cloud storage and stays as is. "Cmdr" is the product name. Sentence case, no full stop. Avoid the words "error" and "failed". Pop-up notice (toast) in the corner of Cmdr's main window.

stateRecovery.keptCopy: Cmdr kept the old file at {path}.

@stateRecovery.keptCopy.description: Line under any of the notices above that a damaged file was set aside rather than deleted, and where. Plain text. Pop-up notice (toast) in the corner of Cmdr's main window.

placeholders.path: the full path of the set-aside copy, like /Users/anna/Library/Application Support/com.veszelovszki.cmdr/settings.json.broken-2026-10-16T101500. Never translated.

@stateRecovery.showInFinder.description: Button on any of the notices above that opens a Finder window with the set-aside copy of the damaged file highlighted. VERB phrase (imperative). ❗ "Finder" is Apple's app name and stays verbatim as "Finder" in every language. Pop-up notice (toast) in the corner of Cmdr's main window.

@stateRecovery.dismiss.description: Button on any of the notices above that closes it. The notice doesn't come back. VERB, imperative, short control label. Pop-up notice (toast) in the corner of Cmdr's main window.
